_datum: Origin = the INSIDE CORNER of the bench top, where the main table and the return meet and where both walls meet. Everything is positive from there. +x runs along the RETURN, away from the back wall, toward where you stand (0..133.5). +y runs along the MAIN TABLE, away from the return corner (0..82). +z is up off the table top; below the bench is -z.
_why_x_is_the_return: Handedness, not preference. From the corner the main table goes one way and the return the other. Putting +x along the MAIN table and +y along the return gives x cross y = -z, a LEFT-handed frame, which silently mirrors the whole cell - that exact mistake was made once already on 2026-07-26 and only the 3D render caught it. Assigning +x to the return and +y to the main table gives x cross y = +z. Verified in code, not assumed.
_measured: 2026-07-26, Kyle. Unmeasured values are null ON PURPOSE - the twin models only what is measured and reports the rest as absent, because a guessed obstacle is worse than a missing one (the gate would report CLEAR against a fiction).

surfaces.name: main
surfaces.notes: The main run. 27.5 deep from the back wall (+x), 82 long from the return corner (+y).

surfaces.name: return
surfaces.notes: The return, 20.25 wide, running out along +x. From the back wall it is 27.5 (the main depth) + 34 = 61.5 to the seam, then 72 more, so 133.5 total - this surface covers x 27.5..133.5.

_walls_note: `height` is the wall's real height above the TABLE TOP. `usable_height`, when present, is how far up is actually reachable - the return side is limited to 34 by ceiling ducts even though the wall itself runs to 48-7/8. Keep them separate: collapsing them would move the wall face the moment someone measures the duct properly. yaw_deg is the direction the wall RUNS (0 = along +x, 90 = along +y); outward is which way the wall MATERIAL sits from its face.

walls.name: back
walls.notes: The MAIN TABLE's back wall, running along +y at x=0, 5 in thick (material occupies x -5..0). 48-7/8 above the table, MEASURED. Starts 8.25 out from the side wall, leaving the corner gap at y 0..8.25. Extends DOWN below the table to its footing; the bottom edge follows the sloping floor. Carries the shelf.

walls.name: side
walls.notes: The RETURN's wall, running along +x at y=0, 5 in thick. PHYSICALLY 48-7/8 above the table; the 34 is USABLE space, cut short by ceiling-mount ducts. Extends DOWN behind the table to its own foundation, bottom edge following the sloping floor.

corner_gap._comment: Gap where the back wall meets the side wall. MEASURED 2026-07-26 at 8.25, so the back wall spans y 8.25..82 and the gap is y 0..8.25.

_legs_note: THE TABLE TOP IS LEVEL AND THE FLOOR IS NOT, so the legs are the only measurement of the floor: differing heights ARE the slope, and the floor plane is solved from them rather than stored - so leg POSITIONS matter as much as heights. x/y are the leg station's CENTRE. `height` is TRUSS HEIGHT: floor to the UNDERSIDE of the table top, excluding the 3/4 top. It is NOT the cut length of a single 2x4 (Kyle, 2026-07-26) - the truss is legs plus rails and no one piece is that long. Do not hand these numbers to a saw. The distinction does not affect the floor: floor-to-underside is exactly what the plane needs. Nominal lumber is not actual lumber: a 2x4 is 1.5 x 3.5. `measured: false` legs have their height INFERRED from the solved floor plane and are EXCLUDED from solving it - otherwise the plane would be fitted to its own output, which is harmless arithmetic today but would silently dilute a real re-measure later.

legs.name: main_outside_corner
legs.notes: Outside (front) corner of the main table at its far end, INSET from both edges - the top overhangs the frame. Inset is 0.5 - MEASURED (Kyle), replacing an earlier 1.0 estimate. Part of a 4-piece 2x4 truss with main_near_back_wall. MEASURED truss height.

legs.name: main_near_back_wall
legs.notes: Far end of the main table, the leg by the back wall. It stands RIGHT IN FRONT OF the footing, not inside it - its back face is on the footing's front face at x=7, so its centre is x 7.75. Part of a 4-piece 2x4 truss with main_outside_corner. MEASURED truss height.

legs.name: return_seam
legs.notes: At the return's seam, 61.5 from the back wall. MEASURED truss height. Inset 0.5 from the return's outer edge. ASSUMPTION: it is on the outer edge rather than against the wall or centred - that choice tilts the solved floor plane, so correct it if wrong. Part of the seam truss.

legs.name: return_end_outside
legs.notes: Return's far-end truss, outside corner. Position inset 0.5 from the return end (x 133.5) and from its outer edge (y 20.25), same construction as the main table's end truss. HEIGHT IS INFERRED from the solved floor plane, not measured - it does not feed back into the floor solve.

legs.name: return_end_wallside
legs.notes: Return's far-end truss, the leg by the side wall. Stands in FRONT of the return footing, whose battered face reaches y=5 at the floor - so its back face is on that, centre y 5.75. HEIGHT INFERRED from the floor plane.

legs.name: return_seam_wallside
legs.notes: Back leg of the SEAM truss, by the side wall. Rotated 90 degrees from leg 3 - it is oriented like the legs in the other trusses, which leg 3 is not (Kyle). Stands in front of the return footing, whose battered face reaches y=5 at the floor. HEIGHT INFERRED from the solved floor plane.

legs.name: return_mid
legs.notes: Extra support leg at the horizontal MIDPOINT between leg 3 (x 61.5) and the return's extent (x 133.5). Oriented like leg 3, not like the trusses' back legs. Standalone - no rails of its own. HEIGHT INFERRED from the solved floor plane. It stands at the under-shelf's mid-span and passes through that level; the real shelf is presumably notched around it.

foundations.name: main_wall
foundations.notes: Concrete footing straddling the main table back wall: 7 into the room, the wall 5, then 7 behind. 9 OFF THE FLOOR END TO END, so it follows the slab slope. Untapered.

foundations.name: return_wall
foundations.notes: The HIGH concrete foundation along the return wall. Its top is LEVEL. The 27 is the height above the floor AT THE RETURN SEAM LEG (x 61.5), which is where Kyle measured it - NOT the height everywhere. The floor drops toward the main table wall, so the block is TALLER than 27 down that end. That is why the measuring point is stored with the number. BATTERED front face: 2 proud of the wall at the top, about 5 at the floor. back 0 puts its rear face flush with the return wall outside edge. ONE SOLID TRAPEZOID - wide at the floor, narrow at the top.

fixtures.name: main_backwall_shelf
fixtures.notes: Shelf on the MAIN back wall, all MEASURED (Kyle, 2026-07-26): 1/2 thick, 12 deep, and 36.5 from the table top to the shelf BOTTOM - so z here, the underside, is +36.5. 50.75 long, starting 3-3/8 inset from the table/wall outside extent (y=82), so it spans y 27.875..78.625. Frame is three half-cut 2x4s: a wall-mounted board along the BACK edge and one under each of the LEFT and RIGHT edges - NO front support, so the front edge is unsupported and the underside is open. Modelled as separate beams below.

fixtures.name: return_undershelf
fixtures.notes: Shelf UNDER the return: its top sits 22 below the return table top (so z, the underside, is -22.5 for a 1/2 thick shelf). Runs from LEG 3 (x 61.5) to the return's extreme end (x 133.5) and is 16 deep. Its back edge is flush with the trapezoid footing's battered face at that height - COMPUTED, not eyeballed: the face is 3.44 proud at x 61.5 and 3.66 at x 133.5, so 3.55 is used and the real edge wanders about 0.11 either side.

features.name: return_seam
features.notes: Where the return's two tops meet, 61.5 from the back wall (27.5 + 34). The return_seam leg lands here.

features.name: return_ceiling_ducts
features.notes: Ceiling-mounted ducts above the RETURN. Not measured, so not modelled - their only recorded effect is the side wall's usable_height of 34. When measured they become a fixture with kind 'duct' (geom group 3, toggleable in the viewer).

features.name: return_wall_foundation
features.notes: A HIGH concrete foundation runs along the return wall, taller than the main wall's. Not measured yet - Kyle said to estimate it later. Deliberately absent rather than guessed.

features.name: floor_drain
features.notes: A drain is visible in the floor photo, consistent with the 2.45 deg slab tilt the leg lengths imply. Not modelled; noted because it explains the slope.

_truss_note: Legs sharing a `truss` name are one braced frame - Kyle's photo shows the far end of the main table as a 4-piece 2x4 truss: two legs, a top rail under the table top, and a bottom rail at the floor. The rails are DERIVED from the leg pair rather than listed, so moving a leg cannot leave its rails behind. ESTIMATE: the bottom rail is placed with its underside on the floor; measure its real height if it matters.

main_far_end._comment: Rails-first frame at the main table's far end. The rails run the FULL length and the posts attach to them (Kyle) - so the posts span BETWEEN the rails rather than floor-to-top. Rails lie FLAT: 1.5 thick vertically, 3.5 across. The TOP rail carries on to the back wall, where it meets the ledger in a half-lap - a 1/2-thickness cutout in the ledger. The lap is joinery, not extent, so the boxes simply overlap.

return_far_end._comment: Same 4-piece construction as main_far_end: rails full length running FLAT, posts attached between them. No top_rail_to_wall - it is at the open end of the return, not against a wall.
return_far_end._bottom_rail: The bottom rail is NOT at floor level here - it doubles as the bearer for the under-shelf, so its top sits at the shelf's underside and the posts carry on down past it to the floor. Referenced to the fixture by name, so moving the shelf moves the rail with it.

return_seam._comment: Truss at the return's seam. Leg 3 is measured; its wall-side partner is inferred. Note the two posts are rotated 90 degrees from each other - that is how it is actually built, not an error.
return_seam._bottom_rail: The bottom rail is NOT at floor level here - it doubles as the bearer for the under-shelf, so its top sits at the shelf's underside and the posts carry on down past it to the floor. Referenced to the fixture by name, so moving the shelf moves the rail with it.

ledgers.name: main_backwall
ledgers.notes: Carries the MAIN table off its back wall. Wide (nominal 4in, actually 3.5) face flat on the wall, so it stands 3.5 tall and projects 1.5 into the room, top flush under the table top. Runs 0..82 - the TABLE's full length, all the way to the return wall (Kyle), which is further than the wall itself runs: the wall stops 8.25 short for the corner gap. Receives the truss top rail in a half-lap.

ledgers.name: return_sidewall
ledgers.notes: Carries the RETURN off the side wall, same construction and orientation, running the return's full 133.5.

beams.name: main_front
beams.notes: Support along the FRONT edge of the main table, running its full length to the return wall (y=0). Inset 0.5 from the table edge; the coordinates here are the beam's centre line.

beams.name: return_front
beams.notes: Support along the FRONT edge of the return, from the main table's front beam (x 27.5) only as far as LEG 3 at the seam (x 61.5) - not to the return's end. Inset 0.5 from the table edge; the coordinates here are the beam's centre line.

beams.name: shelf_back_cleat
beams.notes: Wall-mounted board along the shelf's BACK edge, half-cut 2x4 (1.5 x 1.75). Top carries the shelf underside at 36.5.

beams.name: shelf_side_left
beams.notes: Support under the shelf's LEFT edge, running the full 12 depth.

beams.name: shelf_side_right
beams.notes: Support under the shelf's RIGHT edge. There is deliberately NO front member - the frame is a U, open at the front.

_beams_note: Edge supports, as opposed to the wall ledgers. Laid FLAT: the wide (3.5) face fastens to the underside of the table top, so each is 3.5 across and 1.5 deep vertically. Kyle corrected these - they were stood on edge, 90 degrees out. A beam may carry an explicit `z` (its TOP surface) - the shelf cleats use it; without one a beam sits under the table top.
_inset_note: ALL inset distances are 0.5 in (Kyle, 2026-07-26) - legs, trusses and edge beams alike. This is MEASURED and replaces an earlier 1.0 estimate, which moved every leg and therefore re-solved the floor plane.

braces.name: shelf_knee_left
braces.notes: 45-degree knee brace under the shelf's LEFT side support, same half-cut 2x4 as the rest of the frame. Meets the side support 8 from the wall (centre), so at 45 degrees it lands on the wall 8 lower. Ends are MITRED at 45 so they sit flush - square against the wall face at x=0 and flat under the frame at z=35 - rather than square-cut and overhanging both.

braces.name: shelf_knee_right
braces.notes: 45-degree knee brace under the shelf's RIGHT side support. Ends are MITRED at 45 so they sit flush - square against the wall face at x=0 and flat under the frame at z=35 - rather than square-cut and overhanging both.

_braces_note: Diagonal members. Beams are axis-aligned, so a 45-degree knee brace needs its own type with explicit 3-D endpoints rather than a beam bent to fit.
_scope: THE PLACE ONLY. Table, walls, floor, footings and framing - measured once and reusable as the base for many bench configurations. What STANDS on the bench (arm, cameras) lives in cell.json, deliberately: placement changes constantly and belongs to a project, the room does not.
